 Wichita State’s Shockers Vote Coalition again recognized for its nonpartisan election
 outreach
 By WSU Strategic Communications
 Courtesy photo 
 The Shockers Vote Coalition hosted a series of deliberative dialogues, voter registration
 drives, civic holiday celebrations and other initiatives designed to provide students
 with nonpartisan information about voting while making civic engagement engaging and fun.   
 For a fourth time, Wichita State University’s voter participation and civic engagement
 efforts earned recognition from the ALL IN Campus Democracy Challenge.   
 Wichita State’s Student Engagement & Belonging , a department within the Division of Student Affairs, led the planning and activities
 that earned the university a spot among 273 colleges and universities named as a 2026 ALL IN Most Engaged Campus for College Student Voting .   
 This year, the Shockers Vote Coalition hosted a series of deliberative dialogues,
 voter registration drives, civic holiday celebrations, and other initiatives designed
 to provide students with nonpartisan information about voting while making civic engagement
 engaging and fun.   
 “The Shockers Vote Coalition empowered students with the knowledge and resources needed
 to make informed decisions at the ballot box while encouraging active participation
 in their communities,” said Loren Belew, Civic Engagement Coordinator, Student Engagement & Belonging. “ Through its programs and events, the coalition increased awareness of the voting process
 and helped cultivate a lasting sense of civic pride and engagement.”   
 Loren Belew
 In March, the coalition partnered with the Kansas Public Finance Center to host a
 discussion on the local sales tax vote, helping students better understand the measure
 and its potential impact on the community.    
 During fall 2026, the Shockers Vote Coalition organized multiple voter registration
 drives and civic engagement programs, including a Civic Engagement Fair, Hamilton
 Movie Screening and Trivia Night, and a Ballots 101 educational event.    
 The coalition also celebrated key civic holidays and events, such as National Voter
 Registration Day, National Vote Early Day, and Wichita State's annual Election Day
 Bash, providing students with opportunities to learn, connect, and participate in
 the democratic process.   
 Wichita State received similar recognition in 2020, 2022 and 2024. ALL IN’s Most Engaged
 Campuses for College Student Voting recognizes colleges and universities making intentional
 efforts to increase nonpartisan democratic engagement and college student voting.   
 About Wichita State University
 Wichita State University is Kansas' only urban public research university, enrolling
 more than 24,000 students between its main campus and the WSU Campus of Applied Sciences
 and Technology (WSU Tech), including students from every state in the U.S. and more
 than 100 countries. Wichita State and WSU Tech are recognized for being student-centered
 and innovation-driven. 
 Located in the largest city in the state with one of the highest concentrations in
 the United States of jobs involving science, technology, engineering and math (STEM),
 Wichita State University provides uniquely distinctive and innovative pathways of
 applied learning, applied research and career opportunities for all of our students.
 The National Science Foundation ranked WSU No. 1 in the nation for aerospace engineering
 R&D, No. 2 for industry- and defense-funded engineering R&D and No. 9 overall for
 engineering R&D. 
 The Innovation Campus , which is a physical extension of the Wichita State University main campus, is one
 of the nation’s largest and fastest-growing research/innovation parks, encompassing
 over 120 acres and is home to a number of global companies and organizations.

 Student Engagement & Belonging
 Through our civic engagement events, Student Engagement & Belonging seeks to engage
 our community and in civic engagement through a series of events to connect students
 to volunteer work, alternative breaks programming, voter engagement initiatives, deliberate
 dialogue events and campus events and celebrations to foster civic pride and engagement
 for our community.
